clinician.trajectory_summary: A 44-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of pruritic rash of the extremities and oral cavity, progressing to other body regions, characterized by well-demarcated, erythematous plaques with fragile vesicles. Initial labs showed hyperglycemia, anemia, elevated HbA1c leading to a diabetes diagnosis, and elevated chromogranin A. Imaging revealed a 3-cm enhancing pancreatic head mass. Pathology confirmed a pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma with vascular and perineural invasion. Serum glucagon levels were significantly elevated, consistent with a glucagonoma.
